translated_text: My dearest Ligninial, July 24, 1940. It's been two days since I received a letter from you. The post office is still quite imperfect. Now I'm starting to lose patience a little—I'd like to leave Ligninial as soon as possible. Everyone is already a bit on edge; there are occasional little arguments between Bela and Paulette and Etienne and Suzanne, and it's not always very pleasant. Also, I don't know when there's nothing useful to do. I think I might be able to just cook for you in the evening and at lunchtime. Listen, my little darling, as soon as you have your pass, come! Darling, if you're coming by train, ask at each station where you have to change trains what the times are for the train in the other direction, so that if we ever have to return by train, we know what times are available. Yes. Fine, they know absolutely nothing at all. For gasoline, Pista tries to do a quest (Samulany) and ask the people of Ligninial for 1 to 2 liters of gasoline.
